**FIX A (PRIMARY, r27 NEW §6.7F) — dbt --select comma vs space set-operators**: iter513 Q4 responder said `--select tag:a,tag:b` is 'OR logic'. WRONG. Canonical (verified at docs.getdbt.com/reference/node-selection/set-operators): COMMA (no space) = INTERSECTION (AND — nodes matching BOTH selectors); SPACE-separated = UNION (OR — nodes matching EITHER). The two have OPPOSITE semantics.

**GREP FINDINGS (FIX A)**: searched `--select|tag:|node selection|intersection|union|--exclude` across all resources. Existing `--select tag:` mentions: r25 line 188 (`dbt run --select tag:hourly_refresh`), r25 line 267 (`dbt run --select events_daily_by_tenant`), r27 line 1133 (UNION SQL — unrelated), r27 line 2166-2167 (source freshness `--select source:app`), r27 line 2344 (`dbt build --select fct_orders`), r27 line 2541/2567 (`dbt seed --select plans`), r27 line 2648/2730/2733/2755 (`dbt test --select test_type:unit` and the `dim_customers,test_type:unit` comma combo — but NO explanation of what the comma means), r27 line 2777 (`dbt run --select fct_orders_daily+`). **NO resource stated the comma=AND/space=OR rule — neither correctly nor incorrectly.** The iter513 Q4 'comma is OR' claim was a **PURE responder fab** filling the gap with cloud-CLI-folklore (most Unix tools comma=list/OR; dbt is the inverted case). Line 2733 had the comma form `dim_customers,test_type:unit` already in-use but un-explained — Haiku had no anchor to know it meant AND.

**FIX B (SECONDARY, r17 metadata-tables section) — Iceberg $snapshots operation values + WHO scope**: iter513 Q3 responder listed only 3 operation values (omitted `overwrite`), claimed MERGE shows as `replace` (wrong — MERGE is `overwrite`; `replace` is compaction), and implied $snapshots shows WHO (no user column exists). Canonical (verified at iceberg.apache.org/spec + iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/spark-writes + trino.io/docs/current/connector/iceberg.html): FOUR operation values — `append` (data files added, none removed); `overwrite` (row-level: MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE that rewrite); `delete` (whole data files removed, no new data); `replace` (rewrite with no logical change — compaction/OPTIMIZE). $snapshots has NO user column. To approximate WHO: `element_at(summary, 'trino_query_id')` -> correlate to Trino query log.

**WEBSEARCH VERIFICATION**: (1) dbt comma=intersection / space=union confirmed via WebSearch result at docs.getdbt.com/reference/node-selection/set-operators: 'Commas with no spaces within an argument define an intersection, and a space between arguments combines their results as a union.' Exact example from docs: 'dbt run --select "marts.finance,tag:nightly" — This only selects resources that satisfy all arguments.' (2) Iceberg operation values confirmed via WebSearch at iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/spark-writes: append = 'Only data files were added and no files were removed'; replace = 'Data and delete files were added and removed without changing table data; i.e., compaction'; overwrite = 'Data and delete files were added and removed in a logical overwrite operation'; delete = 'Data files were removed and their contents logically deleted'. Also confirmed 'Iceberg supports MERGE INTO by rewriting data files that contain rows that need to be updated in an overwrite commit' — MERGE -> overwrite definitively. (3) Trino $snapshots columns at trino.io/docs/current/connector/iceberg.html — search results confirm snapshot_id, parent_id, operation are columns but no user/principal column is listed (consistent with our existing line 933/1034/1046 canonical list of six columns). All SQL in edits is valid Trino 467: element_at(map, key) is the canonical NULL-safe map accessor (NOT map[key]); ORDER BY DESC, LIMIT, DATE/TIMESTAMP literals are all standard.
